## Natural history notes

A native perennial wildflower characterized by narrow, lance-shaped leaves and delicate white five-petaled flowers marked with fine purple veins near the center. White Bog Violet occurs in wet, acidic habitats such as bogs, wet flatwoods, marsh edges, seepage areas, and other seasonally saturated sandy soils. In Florida, it is most often associated with open, sunny wetlands where competition from taller vegetation is limited. It flowers mainly in spring and early summer, and its blooms are visited by small native bees and other insects. Like other violets, its foliage can also serve as a larval food source for fritillary butterflies.
